campbell-county-public-library-cold-spri.quote: The Campbell County Public Library Outreach Department offers a variety of services to give homebound residents of Campbell County access to the library's resources. Read about some of our Adult Outreach services below. If you'd like to set up one of these services, call our Adult Outreach Services Assistant at 859-572-5035, ext. 352. Book Talks Our Adult Outreach Services Assistant is available to host monthly book talks at senior centers, adult day care facilities, retirement living homes and extended care facilities. This service differs from a book club in that no particular book is selected to be read by each participant. Instead, topics of interest vary and a presentation is given to educate attendees and encourage intellectually stimulating discussion. Deposit Collections Deposit collections are books loaned to nursing homes, senior centers and other community agencies throughout Campbell County. Collections of 20-30 items are specially selected for each site. Deposit collections may contain an assortment of large print and regular print books, magazines, audiobooks, CDs and DVDs. These collections are delivered on a rotating schedule every four weeks, depending on the facility's needs. Home Delivery Service If you are a resident of Campbell County and cannot visit the library because of temporary or permanent illness or disability, you are eligible for our home delivery service. Materials available for delivery include regular print books, large print books, magazines, DVDs, audiobooks and CDs. Materials are selected based on your reading interests and needs. The Adult Outreach Services Assistant will deliver the materials to your home on a specified day. You may also sign up to have your materials delivered by mail for free.

Consider scheduling your next birthday party by reserving a shelter and ordering from the party menu! No outside food permitted in the facility. See the concession menu for more information. General Facility Policies NO COOLERS permitted in the facility. NO outside food or drinks are allowed in the facility. Food or drink permitted in authorized areas only. Do not leave belongings at concession tables. Concession tables are for eating and drinking. Infants and toddlers are required to wear rubber pants over swim diapers. Swim diapers must be worn due to The Center for Disease Control recommendations. NO Smoking within the facility. If you leave to smoke be sure to have your hand stamped to return at no charge. Children must be with a responsible person 16 years or older. Proper swim attire required (no cut off shorts, jeans, etc.) unless prohibited by religious beliefs. NO running and NO horseplay. Spitting, spouting of water, blowing the nose, or otherwise introducing contaminants into the facility water is not permitted. Diving in shallow water is not permitted. Caution shall be exercised in the use of diving boards. Admission to the facility is refused to all persons having any contagious disease, infectious conditions, & open wounds. Flotation devices permitted, however, a parent/guardian must supervise within an arms reach of their children. City is not responsible for lost or stolen articles. No firearms and/or weapons are permitted in the facility. A valid concealed carry permit does not authorize anyone to carry a concealed weapon onto facility grounds. The facility may not open or may close if the air temperature is 68 degrees or below, or at the discretion of the manager based on inclement weather or because of a fecal accident. Please call 647-4619 or 647-5439 if you have any doubt about the facility being open. The facility may also be closed per the Northern Kentucky Health Department for health related issues. Lightning Policy When a thunder and/or lightning are first noticed the pool will be evacuated until thirty minutes after the last thunder is heard.

Emotional Support / Comfort Animal Policy Dogs whose sole function is to provide comfort or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the ADA. Your needs will determine when and where Travel Training is held. We offer day classes to work with your schedule. Training is usually held on the particular route you would use. Types of Training Trip Training Participants in this type of training work one-on-one with a Travel Trainer to practiced using buses to travel to locations they visit on a regular basis. During Trip Training sessions, participants will learn how to recognize landmarks to know when to get off the bus and how to interact with transit personnel and other riders. Individual Orientation Participants in this type of training will work one-on-one with a Travel Trainer to receive a general introduction to bus accessibility. The goal of Individual Transit Orientation is to educate participants on how to use the entire transit system. During Individual Transit Orientation sessions, a Travel Trainer will explain how to use accessibility features in transit vehicles and how to plan trips on TANK. In addition, Travel Trainers may take participants to a bus garage to practice boarding transit vehicles or practice using buses to build confidence. Group Transit Orientation This type of training provides group presentations at agencies that serve people with disabilities and older adults throughout the three county regions. The goal of Group Transit Orientation is to give participants and agency staff an introduction to the accessibility of TANK, and to demonstrate the benefits of using fixed route buses. During Group Transit Orientation presentations, a Travel Trainer will explain how to use accessibility features in transit vehicles, how to plan trips, pay fares on TANK and how to travel safely in the community while using buses. What does Travel Training involve? Planning your trip Riding specific routes Reading and understanding route maps and schedules Learning how to get to and from your bus stop Understanding the fare structure and how to purchase fare medium Getting on and off the bus safely Transferring to other buses Street crossing Stranger awareness Safety skills Learning to travel independently and with confidence on the bus Is there a cost for Travel Training? There is no charge for Travel Training, but the standard bus fares do apply when riding the bus.

Planning your trip Riding specific routes Reading and understanding route maps and schedules Learning how to get to and from your bus stop Understanding the fare structure and how to purchase fare medium Getting on and off the bus safely Transferring to other buses Street crossing Stranger awareness Safety skills Learning to travel independently and with confidence on the bus Is there a cost for Travel Training? There is no charge for Travel Training, but the standard bus fares do apply when riding the bus. Get Started Today! To request Travel Training services or to find out more please call CJ Grote in the Travel Training office at (859)- 814-2135 or fill out our online form and we will get back to you within 24 hours.

What is TANK Plus? TANK Plus is a flexible, on-demand way to get around town, curb-to-curb within our designated zones…or connecting you to our fixed route service to travel outside of the zones. Instead of fixed bus routes, we use smaller vehicles that you can schedule when you need a ride, either through the TANK+ app or our call center. It’s all about making your transit experience more personalized and convenient. *Please note, curb-to-curb means you would need to walk to the end of your driveway or a designated location to be picked up. The driver will not pull into driveways.
Are vehicles accessible to people with wheelchairs? Yes, you can select wheelchair in the app when booking, or notify the driver at pick up. Each TANK Plus vehicle has space for three wheelchairs.

Service Improvements Go into Effect Nov. 7, 2026 The changes reflect rider and community feedback and will deliver more reliable trips, more frequent service on key routes, better regional connections and support long-term sustainable operations. What’s changing? Starting Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, riders will see the following service improvements: Route 1 will be extended to Newport with service ending at St. Elizabeth Healthcare in Ft. Thomas and will operate as a standalone service (no longer interlined with Route 25). Routes 3, 7 and 12 peak frequencies will increase to every 30 minutes Southbank Shuttle and Route 16 will be replaced with a new high-frequency corridor connecting downtown Newport, Covington and downtown Cincinnati with service provided by a fixed-route bus. Service will operate every 7-8 minutes along the areas currently served by Route 1, interlined Routes 3/12 and interlined Routes 7/25, and every 15 minutes along areas served by Route 1 and interlined Routes 7/25. Riders who currently use Route 16 will have access to the new Route 1 and the Licking River Link as alternative service options.
The TANK Plus zone will expand to include the Alexandria Walmart and Village Green Shopping Center, with a six-mile distance cap designed to improve trip efficiency.
In Covington: Greenup Street at 9th Street Greenup Street at 5th Street Scott Street at 6th Street Scott Street at 11th Street

On fixed route service, TANK announces all transfer points, major intersections, destination points and other intervals along a route to permit individuals with visual impairments or other disabilities to be oriented to their location. These announcements may be made electronically or be made by the bus operator over the PA system.
Drivers will also call out any stop upon request, if you ask when you get on the bus.
